Class User

java.lang.Object
edu.ntnu.idi.bidata.User
public class User extends Object
Entity class representing the user in the application.

Role and Responsibility

The User class represents a registered user who can log in to the diary application, create diary entries, and manage their own content. It links an Author identity (for diary entries) with authentication credentials (username and password).

Key responsibilities include:
  • Storing user identity information (author, username)
  • Managing authentication credentials (hashed password)
  • Providing password verification for login
  • Enabling password changes for logged-in users
Information Stored and Data Type Justification
  • Author (author): The author linked to the user profile is stored as an Author because this makes it possible to create a link between diary entries and their creators. It also allowes for tracking of entry count per author.
  • Username (username): Usernames are textual identifiers. String is the natural choice for variable-length text that needs to support comparison operations.
  • Password (password): Storing the hashed password as a string. Using String makes it easy to compare passwords. The acctual password is never stored in clean text.
Mutability Assessment

The author, username and password is set at creation by the user of the application. The author and username are final, and will not be changed. The password however can be changed later.

Invalid Data Handling Strategy

This class uses a fail-fast exception strategy for critical data:

  • Blank username: The constructor throws IllegalArgumentException with the message "Every user needs to have a username". Usernames are essential for authentication and must not be empty.
  • Blank password: The constructor throws IllegalArgumentException with the message "A password is required to protect your profile". Passwords are essential for security.
  • Null author: No explicit validation is performed for null authors. If null is passed, subsequent operations like getName() will throw NullPointerException. The calling code (UserRegister) ensures valid authors are provided.
  • Password changes: The setNewPassword method accepts any string without validation. The calling code should ensure the new password is properly hashed before setting.
